rooms.2341: Wilderness Way comes down off the open plains here, a rutted cart track pressed between drifts of yellow-flowered gorse. North, the road climbs back toward the Plains under a wide and windy sky, and south the Way runs on along the edge of the grass country. East, the grass grows suddenly enormous, a wall of green stems taller than a mounted rider, and a trodden gap leads in among them. A leaning post of grey oak marks the crossing, its carved arrow worn almost smooth.
rooms.101007: Stems as thick as a man's wrist rise on every side and bend together overhead, so that the grass forms a long green hall with only glints of daylight in its roof. The light is still bright here from the open Way, which shows as a pale gap to the west. A trampled lane runs east deeper into the grass, and a narrower run opens south. The ground is hard and dusty, scattered with the husks of old seed.
rooms.101017: The grass roof hangs lower here, its heavy seedheads nodding down until they brush your shoulders and leave a dust of golden pollen. Wind moves through the tops in a long hiss, and the whole green ceiling heaves and settles like the breath of some vast animal. Lanes lead off east and west through the stems, and a gap to the south shows another hall of grass. Underfoot the soil is dark and springy with old roots.
rooms.101027: A grey boulder the size of a haycart squats in the middle of this grass hall, its top worn smooth and its flanks crusted with orange lichen. The stems have grown up close around it and folded over its crown, so that it sits in green shade like something kept indoors. Lanes run east and west past the stone, and a narrow way leads south. The air smells warm and sweet, like a hayloft at the end of summer.
rooms.101005: Here the stems grow in clumps, and between them the floor is a soft mat of flattened grass pressed into round hollows where large beasts have lain to rest. Coarse hairs, brown and black, are snagged on the lower stalks. Light falls through the roof in a hundred thin gold needles that tremble whenever the wind passes over. The way continues east and west, and a lane opens to the south.
rooms.101015: The grass here has a silver cast, its long blades furred underneath so that the whole hall shimmers pale whenever the wind turns them. A shallow dew pond lies in a dip of the floor, ringed with cracked mud and the sharp prints of hooves. Lanes lead east and west along the length of the grass country, and a gap opens south. The light is cool and watery, as if it came through frosted glass.
rooms.101025: The stems press in close on both sides, leaving a corridor no wider than a cart, its roof so dense that the light comes through a dim, deep green. No side ways open here, and the grass walls are too thick and tough to push through. The lane runs on east and back west. Somewhere above, the wind roars across the tops with the sound of distant surf, yet down here hardly a blade stirs.
rooms.101004: The corridor widens into a round chamber of grass where someone long ago cut the stems back and laid a ring of fieldstones for a fire. The hearth is cold and choked with blown seed, and the stalks around it have grown back scorched black at their feet. Ways lead east and west, and a broad lane opens south into a wider stretch of the grass country. A faint smell of ancient ash still lingers.
rooms.101014: Russet grass grows here, its tall stems stained the colour of rust and its plumes heavy and dark, so that the hall beneath is dim, warm and faintly red. Fallen seed lies ankle-deep along the walls and crunches underfoot. The lanes run east and west, and another leads south between two especially tall clumps. The wind's voice is low here, a long and steady murmur in the roof.
rooms.101024: The grass hall ends at a tangle of fallen, rotting stems, and beyond it the way narrows to a slot that is easy to miss. Someone has notched a few of the stalks beside it with a knife, small marks at knee height that only a searching eye would find. That faint path leads east into deeper shadow, while the open lane runs back west. The air smells strongly of crushed green sap.
rooms.101090: The path threads between stems that have been bent and tied together overhead with twists of cord, forming a low tunnel that someone keeps in quiet repair. The floor is beaten hard by many boots, though fresh-cut grass has been strewn over it to hide the trail. East, the tunnel goes on toward a smell of woodsmoke and horses, and west it rejoins the open grass. A gap low in the wall leads south into another hall of grass.
rooms.101091: The path runs straight here, roofed with old canvas stretched over a frame of ash poles and weighted with stones against the wind. Small iron bells hang on a cord along the roof, placed so that anyone walking through must brush against them. East, a palisade of sharpened stakes shows at the end of the tunnel, its gate standing open into the mercenaries' camp. West, the path leads back into the grass.
rooms.101092: This is the hiring hall of the Rahn Mercenary Camp, a long tent of patched brown canvas raised on stout poles and floored with rough planks. A trestle table runs across the far end, its top scarred with knife cuts and stained with ink and ale, and behind it hangs a banner showing a black fist gripping a sword. Racks of spears and shields line the walls, and a board pinned with written contracts leans by the entrance. The only way out is west, back down the hidden path.
rooms.101021: The grass here grows in dense tufts of blue-green, stiff as broom straw, and the wind whistles thinly through them in the roof. A narrow way leads north to a low gap where the stalks have been bent and tied, and the hall runs south along the edge of the grass country. West, a lane opens into a broader hall. The prints of shod horses cross the soft ground, all of them heading the same way.
rooms.101051: Thistles as tall as the grass itself have taken root here, their purple heads nodding high among the stems and their spiny leaves crowding the floor. A path winds between them north and south, and a wider way opens west. The light is a soft purple-green, and thistledown drifts down through it like slow snow. The ground is dry and stony, the soil lying thin over buried rock.
rooms.101081: The grass country ends here in a blind corner, walled by stems so old and thick that they have grown woody, like a hedge of green canes. Nothing passes them, and the lanes turn away north and west. A shallow scrape in the floor holds a bed of dry grass and a few white bones, gnawed clean. The air is close and smells faintly of musk.
rooms.101071: A wide, low hall stretches here, its roof sagging so close overhead that you must stoop beneath the heaviest seedheads. The floor is crisscrossed by narrow trails no higher than a dog, running off under the walls of stems. Lanes lead east, west and north. The light is dim and gold, and every gust sends a patter of loose seed down onto your shoulders.
rooms.101041: Four lanes meet in this grassy crossing, where the stems have been grazed back into a wide round room with a high, airy roof. A post of weathered wood stands in the middle, its top hung with a bleached horse skull that someone fixed there long ago. Lanes run off north, east, south and west, all looking much alike. When the wind gusts, it moans faintly through the empty eye sockets of the skull.
rooms.101011: The grass here is young and very green, sprung up from ground that was burned not many seasons ago, and its roof is thin enough to glow almost white. Charred stubs of older stems still poke from the soil between the new shoots. Lanes open east and west, and a broad way leads south to a crossing. The air smells of fresh sap and, more faintly, of old smoke.
rooms.101001: A low mound rises from the floor of this grass hall, round and grassed over, with a ring of half-buried stones set about its foot. The stems lean in over it as if listening. Lanes lead east and west along its sides, and a narrower way goes south. No one has disturbed the mound, and the grass upon it grows finer and paler than anywhere around.
rooms.101031: Clumps of feathery pampas grow here among the common grass, their great plumes leaning together overhead into a soft, cream-coloured ceiling. When the wind stirs them they shed a fine fluff that hangs in the air and catches the light. Ways lead off north, east, south and west. The floor is cushioned with the plumes of many years.
rooms.101061: The floor dips here into a long, damp hollow where reeds have crept in among the grass, and the soil squelches black underfoot. A thin trickle of water seeps from one side and pools at the bottom before soaking away. Lanes climb out of the hollow north, east and west. The air is cool and smells of mud and mint, and the light comes greenish through reed and grass alike.
rooms.101050: The stems here are banded green and yellow like a snake's skin, an odd kind of grass that grows nowhere else nearby, and they rattle drily together in the roof. Wide lanes open north, south, east and west. A hunter's mark, three slashes in a triangle, has been cut into a cluster of stalks at eye height. The floor is bare, hard-packed earth.
rooms.101020: A great anthill rises waist-high in this grass hall, a hard dome of red earth long abandoned and crumbling at its crown. The grass grows thin around it, and more light reaches the floor here, warm and yellow. Lanes run north, south, east and west from the clearing about the mound. The red dust of the old hill has stained the nearby stems up to their knees.
rooms.101084: This hall of grass is tall and narrow, its stems so straight and high that the roof seems as far above as the rafters of a temple. Wind howls through the tops, but at the floor the air barely moves and is close and warm. Lanes lead east and west, and a way opens south. A rusted plough blade lies half-buried in the soil, left by some farmer who once tried to tame this ground and lost.
rooms.101074: The grass stands in thick, rounded tussocks here, each one a small green tower, and the lanes between them twist and double back on themselves. Paths open north, south, east and west, though the tussocks make it hard to keep your bearings. The light flickers as the roof sways, and the shadows of stems slide to and fro across the floor. The ground between the tussocks is soft and loamy.
rooms.101044: A fallen tree trunk, silver with age and hollow along its length, lies across this grass hall, carried here by some flood or storm long before the grass grew up around it. The stems have pushed up through its broken ends and split bark. Lanes lead north, south and west, and the trunk must be clambered over to go any way at all. The old wood smells of dry rot and wild honey.
rooms.101034: The grass grows in rows here, straight lines of stems with even lanes between them, as though the field was planted long ago and left to run wild. The roof is high and regular, and the light falls in long bars down each lane. Ways lead north, east and south. At the end of one row stands a toppled stone marker, its face weathered past reading.
rooms.101064: Wild barley has seeded itself among the grass here, its bearded ears hanging thick from the roof and scratching at your face as you pass. A sweet, dusty smell fills the hall. Lanes lead off north, south, east and west, the western one sloping gently downhill. Small shrivelled ears lie scattered over the floor where the wind has shaken them loose.
rooms.101000: The grass hall widens into an almost square room, its walls of stem so straight they look trimmed. A ring of pale, fat mushrooms circles the middle of the floor, and the grass inside the ring is greener than the rest. Lanes leave the room through each of its four walls, north, south, east and west. Travellers seem to step around the ring rather than through it, and their trodden path curves plainly to one side.
rooms.101010: Bindweed has climbed the stems here and knitted them together with its pale trumpet flowers, so that the roof is a white-starred weave letting in a soft, even light. The flowers smell faintly of almonds in the warmth. Lanes lead north, south, east and west, each one hung with trailing tendrils that must be brushed aside. Underfoot the earth is dry and crumbles into dust.
rooms.101040: An old stone well stands in this grass hall, its round wall built of fieldstones and its mouth covered by a rotting wooden lid. The stems have crowded right up against it, and a few have sprouted from the cracks in its masonry. Lanes run north, south, east and west. A cold breath rises through the gaps in the lid, smelling of deep water and wet stone.
rooms.101070: Here the grass grows a darker, wetter green, and the ground slopes very gently toward the forest country to the south. Lanes cross the hall north to south and east to west, worn into shallow ruts by the passing of many hooves. Big drops of dew hang from the roof long into the day and fall with a soft patter. The air carries a first faint scent of leaf mould and pine.
rooms.101080: The grass hall turns and narrows here, and the roof drops low and dense, so that the light takes on the colour of pond water. A cairn of piled stones, knee-high and topped with a flat slab, stands beside the lane where travellers have each added a pebble for luck. Ways lead north, south and west. The wind sounds far away, as if the grass had stopped its ears.
rooms.101023: The lane runs south along the edge of the grass country here, toward a line of darkness that is the eaves of the great forest. The stems on this side grow shorter and patchier, and here and there gaps in the roof are filled with the green of distant treetops. Ways lead north back into the deeper grass and west into a neighbouring hall. Fallen oak leaves, blown far out of the woods, lie scattered among the stems.
rooms.101053: Brambles have crept into the grass here from the woods, weaving thorny arches between the stems and roofing the lane in a dark, prickly lattice. Blackberries ripen among them in season, and old purple stains mark the floor beneath. The lane runs north and south, and a gap in the brambles opens west. Tufts of wool and fur hang snagged on the thorns at shoulder height.
rooms.101083: The last of the grass country thins out here into a ragged hall of short, straggling stems, with the trunks of great trees showing through its far wall. A trodden path leads south out of the grass and over open ground toward the eaves of the Great Forest of MiNar. North, the lane runs back between the tall stems, and another hall opens west. The air is cooler and damper here, and smells of the forest.
rooms.14817: Open ground of short turf and scattered gorse lies here at the corner of the forest, where the grass country gives way to the first great trees. North, a path climbs back toward the towering stems of the grasslands, and south the eaves of the forest run on in a long green wall. West, the forest's edge bends away out of sight. The wind comes freely here, carrying seed from the grass and leaves from the woods together.
rooms.14818: A ditch and bank, overgrown and soft with moss, runs along the forest's edge here, dug long ago by someone who wished to mark where the wild began. Beyond the ditch the trees stand tall and close, and a gap in the bank lets you west into the Great Forest of MiNar. The eaves run on north and south. Outside the trees, rough pasture rolls away under the open sky, dotted with gorse.
rooms.14819: Hawthorn grows thick along the eaves here, its twisted trunks leaning out from under the taller trees as if to escape their shade. In spring the hedge foams with white blossom, and in autumn it hangs heavy with dark red haws. A path runs north and south along its foot, and a gap between two thorns leads west into the woods. A pair of old stone gateposts stand beside the gap with no gate between them.
rooms.14820: The ground rises into a low hummock here, giving a long view over the open country beyond the forest, a patchwork of rough grass and heather fading into haze. Behind you the trees stand dark and tall, and a deer trail slips west between their trunks. The eaves stretch away north and south. The wind blows steadily across the hummock, flattening the heather.
rooms.14821: A great beech has fallen outward from the forest here, its roots torn up in a wall of earth and stone taller than a man and its crown lying broken in the open grass. The path along the eaves bends around the root plate, continuing north and south. West, the gap the beech left in the forest's edge lets a broad wedge of sunlight into the woods. Bracken has sprung up thickly in the new light.
rooms.14822: Silver birches stand along the forest edge here, slender and white against the darker trees behind, their small leaves shivering in every breath of wind. The turf beneath them is short and starred with yellow tormentil. The eaves run north and south, and a narrow way leads west under the birches into the forest proper. Strips of papery bark curl from the trunks and flutter like pale ribbons.
rooms.14823: A spring rises at the foot of an old oak here and spills out of the forest in a clear little stream that wanders away across the open land. Someone has set a flat stone across the trickle as a step, and its top is worn into a shallow dish by many feet. The path along the eaves runs north and south, and a way leads west beside the stream into the trees. The water tastes cold and faintly of iron.
rooms.14824: The eaves are ragged here, the forest's edge broken by a stand of dead pines, grey and leafless, that some long-ago fire killed without felling. Their bare branches creak against one another in the wind. The path runs north and south along the edge, and a way leads west past the dead pines into the living woods. The ground is black and gritty, and fireweed grows tall among the stumps.
rooms.14825: Bracken grows shoulder-high along the edge of the forest here, a rustling sea of brown and green that hides the ground entirely. A path has been trodden through it, running north and south between the trees and the open country. West, the bracken thins beneath the shadow of the first oaks. The air is warm and carries the dry, peppery smell of the fronds.
rooms.14826: A tumbledown hut of stacked turf and branches leans against the trunk of an elm at the forest's edge, the shelter of some woodcutter or charcoal burner long gone. Its roof has fallen in, and nettles fill the doorway. The path along the eaves continues north and south, and a cart track, nearly grown over, leads west into the woods. Old chips of wood, grey and soft, still litter the ground.
rooms.14827: The forest edge curves inward here to form a shallow bay of grass, sheltered by tall trees on three sides and open to the country beyond. The turf is cropped short, and the trees around it bear rubbed and frayed bark at the height of a stag's antlers. The eaves run on north and south, and a well-used trail leads west into the forest. The air in the bay is still and warm.
rooms.14828: A lone standing stone, taller than a man and leaning a little toward the trees, rises from the turf at the forest's edge here. Its sides are scored with deep grooves where generations of boar and deer have scratched themselves. The path runs north and south along the eaves, and a gap opens west into the forest. Lichen in pale green rosettes covers the weather side of the stone.
rooms.14829: Holly grows dense and dark along the eaves here, its glossy leaves shining and its branches so thick that the forest behind is hidden from view. A tunnel-like gap in the holly leads west into the woods. The path continues north and south along the edge, where the turf is scattered with prickly dead leaves. Beyond the forest, open country stretches away grey-green and empty.
rooms.14830: The ground along the forest edge is soft and boggy here, fed by water seeping out from under the trees, and tufts of rush and cotton grass grow in the wet. Planks have been laid end to end along the path to keep feet dry, though several have rotted through. The way runs north and south, and a firmer track leads west onto higher ground among the trees. The smell of peat and wet moss hangs over everything.
rooms.14831: Tall foxgloves stand in purple spires along the eaves here, crowding the sunny margin between the open country and the forest shade. The trees behind are mostly oak, broad and low-branched. The path runs north and south between them and the open land, and a gap leads west under the oaks. The spires nod and bob whenever the wind finds them.
rooms.14832: An old boundary wall of drystone runs along the edge of the forest here, mossy and broken, with whole stretches of it fallen into green heaps. Ferns grow from its chinks, and ivy pours over its top. The path follows it north and south, and a breach in the wall lets you west into the trees. Whoever built it meant to keep something in or out, but the forest has long since won.
rooms.14833: Wild cherry trees grow at the forest's margin here, their bark banded red and shining, and in spring their white blossom drifts out across the open ground like snow. The grass beneath them is long and uncut. The path along the eaves runs north and south, and a narrow way leads west among the cherries into the darker woods. Small hard stones from old fruit crunch underfoot.
rooms.14834: A shallow gully cuts down out of the forest here, carrying a stream that has worn through the soil to grey pebbles and bare rock. A fallen log bridges it where the path along the eaves crosses, running north and south. West, a way climbs the gully's bank into the forest. The stream chatters noisily over its stones before spreading out into the open land.
rooms.14835: Towering ash trees line the forest's edge here, their pale grey trunks rising straight and their feathery leaves letting a dappled light through to the ground. Seed keys hang in brown bunches from the twigs and spin down when the wind blows. The path runs north and south, and a way leads west into the forest under the ash. Out beyond the eaves, the land falls gently away into wide, rolling heath.
rooms.14836: A hunter's high seat, a rickety platform of poles lashed to the trunk of a sycamore, overlooks the open ground at the forest's edge here. Its ladder has lost most of its rungs, and moss covers the planks. The path along the eaves continues north and south, and a way leads west under the sycamore into the trees. The grass about the platform's foot is trampled by hooves.
rooms.14837: Gorse and broom grow thick at the forest's margin here, a blaze of yellow in season and a tangle of green spines the rest of the year. Their sweet scent hangs heavy on warm days. The path squeezes north and south between the bushes and the trees, and a way leads west into the forest. Beyond the gorse, the open country stretches away pale and windswept.
rooms.14838: A rough cart track comes up to the forest edge here and simply stops, as though its makers turned back at the sight of the trees. Its ruts are full of rainwater and its middle is grown with grass. The path along the eaves runs north and south, and a narrow trail continues west into the woods where the carts would not go. A broken wheel lies sunk in the mud at the end of the track.
rooms.14839: The forest edge bends toward its corner here, and the trees grow lower and wind-bent, their crowns all leaning away from the open country. Heather grows right up to their roots in purple drifts. The path runs north along the eaves and south toward a road, and a trail slips west among the stunted trees. The wind blows harder here, sharp and smelling of open land.
rooms.14840: A great oak marks the corner of the forest here, and beside it a gravelled road runs south to the Kalveh Gatehouse, a squat tower of grey stone guarding the way into Baron Kalveh's lands. Its iron gate is shut and chained, the bars rusted, and no warden answers a call. North, the path runs back up the forest's edge, and west it follows the eaves along the trees' far flank. Weeds grow unchecked through the gravel.
rooms.14841: The path along the lower edge of the forest begins here, hugging the trees where a long bank of heather and bilberry slopes away into open moorland. East, the way leads to the great oak at the forest's corner and the road beside it. A trail climbs north into the woods, and the eaves run on west. The ground is peaty and dark, and the bilberry bushes hang with small blue-black fruit in season.
rooms.14700: Just inside the eaves the trees are wind-shaped and stunted, their trunks twisted and their branches all leaning the same way, as though bowing to some old command. Heather gives way here to moss and the first beds of wood sorrel. East, light shows bright where the trees end, and the edge path lies south through a gap. The deeper woods rise north and west, taller with every step.
rooms.14701: The trail that began at the end of the cart track winds through a stand of young hornbeams here, their grey trunks fluted like temple columns. The ground is firm and dry, littered with crisp brown leaves that cling to the twigs through the winter. Ways lead north and south along the inside of the forest edge, and the trail runs on west into the deeper woods. East, the trees thin toward the open eaves.
rooms.14702: Old yews grow in a dark cluster here, their reddish trunks split and hollowed with age and their dense needles shutting out most of the light. Nothing grows beneath them but a thin carpet of needles and fallen red berries. East, brightness and the scent of gorse drift in from the forest edge. Ways lead north and south between the yews, and a darker passage runs west.
rooms.14703: A sycamore of great size spreads its limbs over a small clearing here, and its winged seeds lie in drifts about its roots. Light falls in soft green pools through the gaps in its canopy. The open eaves show east, and the woods continue north, south and west. The ground is rich and black, crowded with young sycamore seedlings fighting for the light.
rooms.14704: Ash and hazel share this stretch of woodland, the tall ash letting down a flickering light and the hazel crowding beneath in a tangle of springy stems. Hazelnut shells, split and empty, crunch underfoot. The eaves lie east, bright through the trees, and the forest runs on north, south and west. A neat line of holes has been drilled up one of the ash trunks by some patient beak.
rooms.14705: The stream that runs out through the gully at the forest's edge passes through here in a deep, fern-hung cleft, gurgling unseen beneath the fronds. A mossy log crosses it, the only dry way over. East, the cleft opens toward the eaves, and the woods continue north and south along the bank and west upstream. The air is cool and damp, and smells of wet stone and liverwort.
rooms.14720: Cherry trees have spread inward from the forest margin here, mingling with oak and lime, and their red-banded trunks stand out among the grey. Lime flowers sweeten the air in summer, and the ground beneath is scattered with cherry stones and fallen leaves. The edge of the forest lies east, and ways lead north, south and west through the mixed woodland. Shafts of sunlight slant down through the canopy.
rooms.14721: The tumbled boundary wall at the forest's edge has a twin here, a second and older line of stones running deeper in among the trees, half sunk in moss and leaf mould. Ivy-covered gaps in it lead east toward the open eaves, north and south along its length, and west into shadow. Ferns crowd its foot, and the stones are cold and wet to the touch. No one remembers who raised either wall, or why.
rooms.14673: Broad, low-branched oaks fill this part of the forest, their limbs reaching sideways more than up, so that the canopy is wide and the light beneath it soft and green. Acorn cups and oak apples litter the ground among patches of bluebells. The eaves and their foxgloves lie east, and the oak wood continues north, south and west. Every low twig has been browsed away to the height of a man's chin.
rooms.14672: The ground is wet and spongy here, with water seeping out from under the moss and gathering in dark pools between the tree roots. Alders grow along the wettest stretches, their roots arching out of the mud like the ribs of a basket. Drier ground lies north and south, a squelching way leads east toward the forest edge, and a rise in the land offers a firmer path west. The air is heavy with the smell of rot and growing things.
rooms.14671: Holly grows thick beneath the taller trees here, a dark understorey of glossy leaves that makes the forest seem dim even at noon. Narrow paths wind through it east to the forest's edge and north, south and west deeper among the trunks. The holly leaves rattle stiffly when anything brushes past them. Beneath the bushes lies a dry, prickly floor where little else will grow.
rooms.14670: A wide, sunny glade opens here among the beeches, its floor a lawn of fine grass kept short by grazing deer. A path leads east through the trees toward the standing stone at the forest's edge, and others go north, south and west into the woods. Beech mast lies thick along the margins of the glade. The open grass is warm and bright, and smells of crushed clover.
rooms.14669: The trees here are old and broad, and many bear long scars where stags have rubbed the velvet from their antlers, the bark shredded and hanging in strips. Deer trails converge from every side, crossing the leaf litter in narrow beaten lines. East lies the sheltered grassy bay at the forest's edge, and the woods continue north, south and west. A musky scent hangs in the still air.
rooms.14667: Coppiced hazels stand in a ragged grove here, each stool sending up a dozen tall straight poles from a single gnarled base, though no one has cut them in many years. Old axe marks still show on the stools. East, an overgrown cart track leads out past a ruined hut toward the forest's edge. The woods run on north and south, and west the hazels give way to taller trees.
rooms.14665: Bracken spills in from the forest's edge and covers the floor here in a rustling green tide, so tall that only the trunks of the oaks rise above it. A narrow track parts the fronds, running north and south, and other gaps lead east and west. Beneath the bracken the ground is hidden, and roots and holes catch at careless feet. The smell of warm, dry fern hangs over everything.
rooms.14663: Fire passed through this part of the forest long ago, and its mark remains in the blackened, hollowed trunks of the oldest trees, still living around their charred hearts. Young birch and rowan have filled the gaps the flames made. East, the dead pines stand grey at the eaves, and ways lead north, south and west among the scarred survivors. Charcoal still shows in the soil wherever the moss has been scraped away.
rooms.14659: A mossy dell dips here among the oaks, and at its bottom water wells up through a bed of green and gold moss to feed the stream that runs east to the spring at the forest's edge. Every stone and root in the dell is cushioned in moss, deep and soft as a feather bed. Ways climb out of the dell north, south and west. The light is green, and the air is hushed and damp.
rooms.14652: Birches march in from the forest's edge and grow here among the darker oaks, their white trunks gleaming in the gloom like candles. Bracket fungi, hard and grey, jut in tiers from the dead ones. The eaves lie east, bright beyond the white trunks, while the forest continues north, south and west. Fallen birch bark curls in pale scrolls upon the ground.
rooms.14645: When the great beech at the forest's edge fell, it tore open the canopy here, and sunlight now pours down into a long, bright gap among the trees. Raspberry canes and foxgloves have sprung up in the light, and the ground is warm. East, the gap runs out to the eaves and the beech's upturned roots. Shaded woods lie north, south and west on either side of the bright gash.
rooms.14635: A deer trail runs through this part of the forest, a narrow beaten line that comes in from the hummock at the forest's edge to the east and winds away west among the trees. Ways also lead north and south. The trees here are a mix of oak and sweet chestnut, and spiny chestnut husks lie split open on the ground. The light is dappled and restless as the leaves move.
rooms.14623: A sunken lane runs between two banks here, so old that the banks have become hedges of ancient hazel and holly meeting overhead. It leads east between the stone gateposts to the forest's edge and west into the trees, worn deep into the earth by the feet of people long gone. Gaps in the banks lead north and south. Ferns sprout from the walls of the lane, and its bed is soft with leaves.
rooms.14611: Just within the ditch and bank at the forest's edge, the trees grow tall and close, mostly oak and beech with a few dark pines among them. A gap in the bank lets out east to the open eaves. Ways lead north toward the corner of the forest, and south and west into the depths. Moss covers the bank in a thick green pelt, and the ground beneath the trees is quiet and soft.
rooms.14816: Here the forest's edge turns its corner, and a strip of open heath runs between the trees and the distant wall of giant grass. Heather and harebells grow in the thin soil, and the wind sweeps across them unhindered. East, the heath leads on to the open ground where the grass country meets the forest, and west the eaves run along the edge of the trees. South, a way slips into the forest between a pair of tall pines.
rooms.14815: A line of old pollarded willows stands along the forest's edge here, their heads bristling with thin shoots and their trunks swollen and hollow. A wet ditch runs at their feet, full of watercress. The edge path continues east and west, and a plank across the ditch leads south into the trees. Out beyond the eaves, the heath rolls toward the far grass country under a wide sky.
rooms.14610: The forest begins in earnest here, just within its edge: tall oaks and beeches crowd together, and the light dims to a green twilight. A plank across a ditch leads north back out to the eaves, and ways run east, south and west among the trunks. Old willow leaves, blown in from the edge, lie yellow on the moss. The air is cool and very still.
rooms.14622: Wood anemones carpet the ground here in spring, white stars spread beneath the bare trees, and later the floor turns to a deep green of their leaves. The trees are tall and smooth-barked, mostly beech, and their roots ripple across the ground like frozen waves. Ways lead north, south, east and west, all beneath the same high, pale grey columns. The silence here is deep.
rooms.14634: A great boulder of grey granite, split clean in two, sits among the trees here, and a young rowan grows from the crack between the halves. The stone is furred with moss on its shaded side and bare and warm on the other. Ways pass it north and south, and paths lead east and west. Red rowan berries lie scattered over the stone in autumn.
rooms.14644: Ferns grow waist-high here, a crowded sea of lady fern and buckler fern whose fronds arch and overlap until no ground can be seen. The trees above are old oaks hung with grey lichen. Trails push through the ferns north, south, east and west. Every step stirs up a cool green smell, and the fronds close silently behind you.
rooms.14651: The ground is laced with roots here, great serpentine roots of beech that coil over and under one another and across the rocks, so that every step must be chosen with care. Hollows between them hold black pools of rainwater. Ways lead north and south between the trunks, and east and west over the roots. The beeches above are vast, their smooth bark carved with initials long since stretched out of shape.
rooms.14658: Below the mossy dell the ground levels into a flat of wood sorrel, its clover-like leaves folding shut in shade and opening wherever a sunbeam strikes. The trees are slim oaks, close-set and straight. East, the dell dips down toward its welling spring, and ways lead north, south and west. The floor is so soft with leaf mould that footsteps make no sound at all.
rooms.14662: A ring of seven old oaks stands here around a bare patch of earth where nothing grows, as if the trees had drawn back to leave room for something. The ground within the ring is packed hard and faintly warm. Gaps between the trunks lead north, south and west, and east toward the old fire scars. Mistletoe hangs in pale green balls high in the oak crowns.
rooms.14664: A little brook comes chuckling through the trees here, clear over brown pebbles, and wanders on between banks thick with marsh marigold. Stepping stones cross it, slick with green weed. Ways lead north and south along its banks and east and west across it. The air is fresh and full of the sound of running water.
rooms.14666: The brook pools here behind a dam of fallen branches and silt, forming a still, dark pond that mirrors the canopy. Water lilies spread across its surface, and the banks are soft and trampled with hoof prints where beasts come down to drink. A path skirts the pond north and south, and ways lead east and west among the trees. The smell of still water and waterweed hangs in the air.
rooms.14668: Below the pond the brook spills over a lip of rock in a little waterfall no higher than a man's knee, and the spray keeps the stones around it green and shining. Ferns crowd every ledge. Ways lead north to the pond, south downstream, and east and west through the woods. The constant splash of falling water fills this part of the forest.
rooms.14707: The brook vanishes here into a crack among the tree roots, swallowed by the earth with a hollow gurgle through a gap far too narrow for anyone to follow. Moss-covered rocks ring the crack, and cold air breathes out of it. Ways lead north back toward the waterfall, and south, east and west through the forest. Lichen grows thick on every trunk here, grey-green and shaggy.
rooms.14708: A dense thicket of young beech saplings fills this stretch, each stem straining upward toward a gap in the canopy left by some fallen giant. Their dry brown leaves hang on through the winter and whisper constantly. Narrow ways lead north and south through the thicket, and east and west where the saplings thin. The remains of the old tree lie half hidden, a long mound of moss and fungus.
rooms.14709: Fungi of every kind sprout from the deadwood here: shelves of orange, clusters of grey bells, and white puffballs the size of a man's head. A heavy, earthy smell rises from the rotting logs. Ways lead north, south and west, and east toward wetter ground near the forest's edge. The light is dim, the canopy closed overhead.
rooms.14741: Two great trees, an oak and a beech, have grown so close together that their trunks have fused at the base into a single massive column, parting again higher up. Travellers call such pairs lovers' trees, and many initials have been cut into the joined bark. Ways lead north, south, east and west around them. Ivy climbs both trunks into the canopy.
rooms.14740: The forest floor is thickly carpeted here with dog's mercury and wild garlic, and the sharp smell of the garlic rises with every step. White starry flowers cover the ground in spring. Ways lead north and south, east toward the old wall in the woods, and west into a darker part of the forest. The trees are tall ashes, letting through a pale, even light.
rooms.14739: A steep bank rises among the trees here, too sheer and crumbling to climb, its face a tangle of bare roots and yellow sand. Ways lead north and south along its foot, and east toward the cherry trees near the eaves. Burrows riddle the sand of the bank in neat round holes. Pebbles trickle down its face whenever the wind stirs the trees above.
rooms.14738: Old pines grow here among the broadleaves, their trunks straight and russet, and a thick bed of needles muffles the ground. Resin seeps in amber beads from old wounds in their bark, and its sharp scent fills the air. Ways lead north and south among the pines, east toward the stream cleft, and west into mist that gathers in a hollow. Pine cones lie scattered everywhere.
rooms.14737: A grassy track, the ghost of an old forest road, runs through here, wider than any deer trail and lined with low banks on either side. Its surface is sunken and green, and saplings grow from its middle. Ways lead north and south through the trees, east along the old road toward the eaves, and west down into a misty hollow. A mossy milestone leans beside the track.
rooms.14710: Honeysuckle and bramble riot over the ground here, tangled together in great mounds between the trunks. The scent of the honeysuckle is heavy and sweet on warm evenings. Narrow ways have been forced through the tangle north, south, east and west. Torn tufts of fur hang in the brambles where beasts have pushed through.
rooms.14711: A clearing opens here where a woodcutter once worked, and a circle of flat stumps, grey and soft with age, stands among the young growth. One great stump in the middle served as a chopping block, and its top is scored with a thousand cuts. Ways lead north, south, east and west from the clearing. Willowherb grows tall and pink in the sun.
rooms.14712: Moss has covered everything here, the ground, the rocks, the fallen logs and the trunks of the trees up to the height of a man, so that the whole wood is green and soft. The light is dim and as green as deep water. Ways lead north, south, east and west through the moss-hung trees. Every sound is swallowed, and the forest feels as hushed as a held breath.
rooms.14713: The forest thins toward its lower edge here, where the trees give way to bracken and the light grows stronger. A path leads south out of the trees to the eaves, and ways run north, east and west through the last of the woods. The trees are crooked rowans and old thorns, gnarled by the wind. A heap of stones, perhaps an old field clearance, lies overgrown among the bracken.
rooms.14842: The eaves run along the forest's lower edge here, and beyond the trees a long slope of moorland falls away toward a far blue line of hills. Bilberry and crowberry cover the ground in a low, springy mat. The path runs east and west along the edge, and a way leads north into the trees between two crooked rowans. The wind off the moor is cold and smells of peat.
rooms.14843: A tumbled cairn of white quartz stands at the forest's edge here, glinting in the light, raised perhaps as a guide for travellers on the moor. The path along the eaves continues east and west. North, a way leads into the forest, where mist hangs among the trees. The ground is rough and stony, and tough tufts of moor grass grow between the rocks.
rooms.14714: Mist collects among the trees here, rising from the damp ground and hanging in pale drifts between the trunks, so that the forest fades into grey only a few paces away. Ways lead north and west into the mist, east through the trees, and south out to the eaves where the light is brighter. Beads of moisture cling to every twig and leaf. The ground is soft and wet.
rooms.14715: The mist lies thick in this hollow of the forest, and the trees loom out of it like grey ghosts, their branches dripping steadily. Roots break the surface of the ground in twisted loops, ready to trip the unwary. Ways lead north, south, east and west, though in the mist each looks much like the others. The only sound is the patter of drops on dead leaves.
rooms.14716: The trees here are ancient oaks, gnarled and hollow, their limbs heavy with grey beards of lichen that hang motionless in the misty air. One has a hollow at its foot large enough for a man to crawl into, though it holds nothing but leaves. Ways lead north, south, east and west among them. The air is cold and smells of wet bark.
rooms.14717: A slow stream creeps through this part of the forest, so sluggish and choked with weed that it barely seems to move. Mist rises from its surface, and its banks are deep black mud. A fallen trunk bridges it, leading north and south, and ways run east and west along its banks. Marsh plants with broad, heavy leaves crowd the water's edge.
rooms.14718: Roots tangle the ground so thickly here that it is like walking on a woven mat, with gaps between them that drop into dark holes. The trees above are huge beeches. Ways lead north and south across the roots, and east toward the old forest road. Beyond the far trunks a thicket of blackthorn rises like a solid wall, too dense to pass.
rooms.14719: The blackthorn thicket hems this pocket of forest closely, its black stems and long thorns forming a barrier that nothing could pass. Within its curve the ground is mossy and sheltered, and mist pools there like water in a bowl. Ways lead north and south along the thicket, and east toward the pines. Sloes hang blue-black on the thorns in autumn.
rooms.14742: A strange stillness lies over this part of the forest, where the trees are tall and straight and the ground beneath them is bare of all but moss. The blackthorn wall continues beyond the trunks, unbroken. Ways lead north and south, and east toward the beds of wild garlic. A single great white stone, smooth as an egg, sits half buried in the moss.
rooms.14725: Old limes grow here, each trunk ringed by a thicket of its own suckers, so that every tree stands in a little grove of its own. In summer the air is heavy with the honey scent of their flowers. Ways lead north and south between the lime groves, and east toward two trees grown into one. The ground is soft with old lime leaves.
rooms.14724: A low ridge of mossy rocks runs through the forest here, broken into stepping blocks and small ledges where ferns grow. The trees cling to it with roots that wrap the stones like fingers. Ways lead north and south along the ridge, and east down toward the fungus-covered deadwood. A cleft between two rocks is packed with dry leaves blown in by the wind.
rooms.14723: A tall dead oak stands here stripped of its bark, its white limbs raised like bones against the green canopy. Its trunk is riddled with holes, some old and some fresh. Ways lead north and south past it, and east toward the beech thicket. Below it the ground is littered with fallen branches, grey and brittle.
rooms.14722: The forest opens a little here where several trails cross, worn by deer and boar into narrow, muddy ruts. A huge wallow of churned mud lies in a low spot, rimmed with coarse bristles where boar have rolled. Trails run off from the crossing north, south, east and west. The smell of mud and beast is strong.
rooms.14692: A pair of standing timbers, the posts of some forgotten gateway, rise here among the trees, black with age and carved with interlacing knots now soft with moss. No fence or wall runs from them, for the forest has swallowed whatever they once guarded. Ways lead north and south between the posts, east toward the little waterfall and west into older woods. The ground is thick with dog violets.
rooms.14687: The trees here are hornbeam and field maple, small and twisted, crowding together beneath a few towering oaks. The maples turn the colour of flame in autumn, and their fallen leaves lie in bright drifts. Ways lead north and south, east toward the brook's still pond, and west into the deeper forest. The ground is uneven, humped with mossy hummocks under the leaves.
rooms.14661: A great hollow oak stands here, its trunk split open on one side to show a dark chamber within, big enough for two people to stand in. The inside is dry and smells of old wood dust. Ways lead north, south and west around it, and east toward the ring of seven oaks. Above the split the tree still lives, its crown broad and green.
rooms.14657: Bluebells flood the ground here in spring, a hazy blue sea beneath the new green of the beeches, and their sweet scent fills the woods. Later in the year the floor is a mass of strappy leaves and rattling seed heads. Ways lead north, south, east and west through the beech wood. The trunks rise grey and smooth, like the pillars of a hall without walls.
rooms.14650: A tiny clearing here holds a forest pool no bigger than a cartwheel, so still and dark that it mirrors the leaves above it perfectly. Mossy stones ring its edge, and its water is clear and very cold. Ways lead north, south, east and west among the surrounding birches and oaks. Fallen leaves float motionless on the surface.
rooms.14643: The ground climbs here onto a low knoll crowned with old pines, their red upper trunks glowing wherever the sun strikes them. The air is dry and resinous, and the needles underfoot are slippery. Ways run down off the knoll north, south, east and west. From its top, the green roof of the forest stretches away farther than the eye can follow.
rooms.14633: Crab apple trees grow among the oaks here, gnarled and thorny, and in autumn their small sour fruit drops to rot in the grass with a sharp, cidery smell. The trees are hung with grey-green lichen. Ways lead north, south, east and west, and the grass between the trees grows long and tangled. In spring the blossom is pink and white.
rooms.14621: A wide ride runs through the trees here, a long open lane once cut through the forest for hunting and now grown up in grass and knapweed. The trees stand back from it on either side like onlookers. Ways lead north toward the forest edge, south along the ride, and east and west into the woods. The grass of the ride is studded with molehills.
rooms.14609: The forest is young here near its edge, a crowd of slim birch, rowan and hazel that has sprung up where older trees once stood. Light comes easily through their thin crowns. North, the trees open onto the eaves, and ways lead east, south and west. Woodbine twines around many of the slender trunks.
rooms.14814: Here the forest's edge is fringed with a broad belt of tall nettles and docks, waist-high and stinging, with a narrow path trodden along it. Beyond, open heath runs toward the distant grass country. The edge path continues east and west, and a gap in the nettles leads south into the trees. Seed heads of thistle and dandelion drift by on the wind.
rooms.14813: A low earth bank topped with gnarled blackthorn runs along the forest edge here, bent by the winds that sweep across the open heath beyond. In spring it is white with blossom before the leaves come. The path follows the bank east and west, and a way leads south through a gap into the woods. Small scrapes and burrows pock the sandy soil of the bank.
rooms.14608: Just within the eaves the trees here are oaks, short and broad, their lower limbs sweeping the ground. Their shade is deep, and the floor beneath is bare earth and leaf litter. North, a gap leads out to the edge of the forest, and ways run east, south and west. Galls like small brown marbles stud the oak twigs.
rooms.14620: Two paths cross here beneath a tall wild pear tree, its trunk rough and dark and its crown laden in autumn with small hard pears. Someone has hung a ring of plaited straw from one low branch, faded and tattered. Paths lead away from the tree north, south, east and west. Fallen pears lie bruised and brown in the grass.
rooms.14632: Wild strawberries carpet the ground in a sunny patch here, their tiny red fruit hiding under trefoil leaves. The trees around are mostly birch, and their light shade lets the sun through. Faint paths cross the patch, running north, south, east and west. The warm air smells sweetly of fruit and crushed leaves.
rooms.14642: The ground falls away here into a shallow ravine, its sides cloaked in hart's-tongue fern and its bottom thick with mossy boulders. A trickle of water runs among the stones. Ways lead north and south along the ravine floor, and east and west up its banks. The air is cool and damp, and the light reaches the bottom only in thin green rays.
rooms.14649: A huge yew stands alone here, its dark crown spreading wide and its trunk split into a dozen fluted stems. Nothing grows beneath it, and the ground is bare, dry and red with fallen needles. Ways lead north, south, east and west from beneath its shade. The yew is old beyond telling, and the silence beneath it feels deliberate.
rooms.14656: A wall of tangled bramble and fallen trees closes the forest off here, piled so high and thick that no way leads on through it. The ground is broken and rough with deadfall. Ways lead north, and east and west along the barrier. Briars hang thickly from the dead branches, and the smell of decay is strong.
rooms.14655: The forest grows dark here, the canopy thick and the trunks of the trees close together. Old pines and yews mix with the oaks, and the ground is soft with needles. Ways lead north, south, east and west, the southern way sloping downhill into deeper shadow. Little light reaches the floor, and the air is cold and smells of resin.
rooms.14648: Cobwebs drape the undergrowth here in great grey sheets, heavy with dew and strung between the bushes and low branches, some of them far too large for any ordinary spinner. The trees are old and dead-limbed, their bark peeling. Ways lead north, south, east and west, though the webs must be pushed aside. The forest is very quiet here, and the air feels close.
rooms.14641: A clearing of short, cropped grass opens here, ringed with hawthorns. In the middle lies a flat stone like a table, worn smooth and stained with the black of old fires. Openings in the ring of hawthorns lead north, south, east and west. The light here is clear and bright after the shade of the deep woods.
rooms.14631: Old beeches stand here with their roots laid bare by the weather, so that the trunks seem to stand on tall, twisted legs above the forest floor. Hollows under the roots are dark and dry. Paths wind between the stilted trunks north, south, east and west. The beech leaves above glow copper in the afternoon light.
rooms.14619: The forest floor here is thick with periwinkle, its shiny dark leaves and blue flowers spreading under the trees in a creeping carpet. The trunks around are oak and ash, tall and straight. Ways lead north toward the eaves, south deeper into the woods, and east and west among the trees. A gentle breeze moves the leaves overhead, setting small shadows dancing.
rooms.14607: Close to the forest's edge the trees are young and the undergrowth dense, a scrub of hazel, elder and dog rose that grows rank in the light from the eaves. Elderflowers smell sweet in summer, and their black berries stain the ground in autumn. North, the way leads out to the forest's edge, and paths run east, south and west through the scrub. The ground is trodden into narrow, muddy runs.
rooms.14812: Along the edge of the forest here a low stone wall, rough and moss-covered, marks off the woods from the open heath. Gaps in the wall lead south into the trees. The path along the eaves runs east and west beside it. The heath beyond is broad and windswept, purple with heather in late summer.
rooms.14811: The forest's edge runs straight here, the trees standing in an even line as if planted, mostly oaks of a great age. Their shade spreads out over the margin of the heath. The path continues east and west along the eaves, and a way leads south into the trees. An old iron horseshoe has been nailed to one of the oaks at head height, rusted almost through.
rooms.14606: The trees grow big here, the first of the old giants of the forest's interior: oaks and beeches so broad that three men could not link arms around them. The ground is open beneath them, carpeted in moss and old leaves. North, the eaves are near, and ways lead east, south and west into the woods. Shafts of sunlight fall between the trunks like pillars of gold.

2341.description: The old oak post leans with the wind. A carved arrow points toward the giant grass, and beneath it someone has scratched the word RAHN and a small crossed-swords mark, newer than the rest.

101001.description: The mound is too regular to be natural, a barrow raised over someone long forgotten. The ring stones are grey and smooth, and one bears a faded spiral cut deep into its face.

101092.description: Contracts in many hands are pinned to the board: an escort wanted for a wool caravan to New Thalos, guards for a warehouse in Port Halyon, two blades for a season in the hills. The terms are the same on every one: half paid in advance, half on return, and a tenth to the Rahn company.

101040.description: The well is old and deep, and its lid has rotted through in places. Far below, a dark gleam of water shows, and a dropped pebble takes a long time to answer with a hollow plop.

14828.description: The stone is rough grey granite, polished smooth where beasts have rubbed against it. High up, above the reach of any deer, a crude stag's head has been pecked into its face by some long-dead hand.

14840.description: The iron gate is fastened with a heavy chain and a padlock furred with rust. A painted board above it once bore the baron's arms, but the paint has flaked away to bare grey wood.

14634.description: The boulder has split as cleanly as if a giant's axe had struck it. The rowan in the crack has thrust its roots deep into the gap, and country folk say a rowan grown from stone keeps evil from the wood about it.

14662.description: The seven oaks stand almost evenly spaced, and the bare earth between them is marked with faint rings, as if many small feet had danced there on summer nights.

14737.description: Scraping back the moss shows a carved number, a worn letter that might be a K, and an arrow pointing along the old road toward the forest's edge.

14742.description: The stone is milk-white and cool even in summer, its surface so smooth it feels polished. Nothing grows on it, not even lichen.

14620.description: The ring of straw is woven in the shape of a wreath, with a twist of red wool tied through it. Country folk hang such things as gifts for whatever dwells in the old woods, so that it will let them pass.

creatures.long_desc: A Rahn mercenary in a scarred leather jerkin waits here, ready to sell his sword to whoever can pay.
creatures.description: He is a hard, weathered man with a close-cropped beard and a nose that has been broken more than once. A black fist gripping a sword is stitched on the shoulder of his jerkin, the badge of the Rahn company. He sizes you up with the calm of someone weighing the price of a job, not the cost of a fight.
rooms: Rahn Mercenary Camp: A Place to Hire

creatures.long_desc: A dun wild horse crops the grass stems here, its ears turning at every sound.
creatures.description: The horse is small and sturdy, sandy brown with a dark stripe down its back and a black, ragged mane. Burrs are tangled in its tail, and its hooves are worn round from the hard ground of the grass country. It watches you with one rolling eye, ready to bolt.

creatures.long_desc: A tawny prairie wolf slinks low between the grass stems, watching you.
creatures.description: This wolf is lean and long-legged, its coat the colour of dry grass so that it all but vanishes among the stems. Its ears are large and its muzzle narrow, and a ridge of darker fur bristles along its spine. It moves with the patience of a hunter that has learned to wait for the herd to stray.

creatures.long_desc: A red stag lifts its antlered head from browsing and regards you warily.
creatures.description: The stag stands tall at the shoulder, its coat a deep russet and its neck thick with a shaggy mane. Its antlers branch into many tines, rubbed clean and pale at the points. Its nostrils flare as it tests the air for your scent.

creatures.long_desc: A grey timber wolf pads silently between the trees, its hackles raised.
creatures.description: The wolf is big and heavy-shouldered, its thick grey coat darkening to black along the back. Old scars cross its muzzle, and its yellow eyes hold you without blinking. Somewhere in the trees behind it, others of its pack are surely waiting.

creatures.long_desc: A shaggy owlbear rears up among the trees, its hooked beak clacking.
creatures.description: The owlbear has the hulking body of a bear covered in a mix of coarse brown fur and ragged feathers, and the round, staring head of a great owl. Its beak is hooked and yellow, and its forepaws end in claws as long as daggers. It reeks of blood and rotting leaves, and its hooting growl is the most terrible sound in the forest.

items.room_desc: A mercenary's leather jerkin lies here in a heap.
items.description: A sleeveless jerkin of thick boiled leather, scarred by old blade cuts and patched at one side. A black fist gripping a sword is stitched on the shoulder.
A broad-bladed knife with a grip cut from the tine of a MiNar stag's antler, smoothed by long handling. The Rahn mercenaries carve these in idle hours at camp.

items.room_desc: A long, hooked claw lies here, crusted with dried blood.
items.description: A black claw as long as a dagger, curved like a sickle and still sharp at the point. Hunters and trophy dealers pay well for such proof of an owlbear slain.

items.room_desc: A tawny wolf pelt lies here, rolled up loosely.
items.description: The pelt of a prairie wolf, coarse and the colour of dry grass. A furrier would give a fair price for it.

items.room_desc: A haunch of venison lies here.
items.description: A dark, lean haunch of red deer, rich-smelling and heavy. It would make a fine meal roasted over a fire.
